A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CROSS and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L. Retained material can be matched reliably across the additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original link-prediction and industrial node-classification results, alongside ablations, robustness experiments, efficiency measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds semantic-dynamics ablations, edge-classification results, and additional link-prediction metrics.

M1.justification: The core extractor, co-encoder, mixer, and training equations remain unchanged. Appendix L.2 adds an edge-classification adaptation using direct supervised training or link-prediction pretraining followed by a fine-tuned two-layer MLP over a frozen encoder.

E1.justification: The five datasets and existing link-prediction and industrial node-classification tasks are retained. Appendix L.2 adds edge classification on Enron, providing a bounded extension of task coverage without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched link-prediction, node-classification, and robustness comparisons. The new edge-classification experiment uses JODIE, DyRep, GraphMixer, and DyGFormer, all already evaluated in v2; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Supplementary metric reporting changes from AUC/Hits@10 to AP/AUC. New experiments introduce temporal-sampling controls and supervised versus frozen-encoder edge-classification protocols, evaluated with precision, recall, and F1. Existing chronological splits, 100-negative-link MRR evaluation, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix L.1 and Table 10 add controlled comparisons using fixed time intervals, summaries of the most recent 20 neighbors, and removal of time encoding on Enron with TGAT and TGN. Existing ablations, robustness tests, parameter studies, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Section D.3 retains three runs with seeds 0–2 and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. However, the new semantic-dynamics and edge-classification Tables 10–11 provide point estimates without standard deviations, limiting uncertainty reporting for these additions. No increase or decrease in run counts is established.

E6.justification: The main MRR results and existing plotted results are unchanged. v3 adds AP results across all five datasets, expands AUC reporting, and removes v2's Hits@10 results. Tables 10–11 add substantive ablation and edge-classification findings; CROSS achieves F1 of 70.91 in supervised classification and 58.29 in the frozen-encoder setting, versus best reported baselines of 64.78 for JODIE and 45.20 for DyGFormer, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds Theorem 2 and its proof, asserting a positive mutual-information improvement bounded using conditional entropies and a constant beta. This substantially extends the formal analysis; the original definitions, Theorem 1 and its proof, and complexity analysis are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about temporal semantic extraction, semantic-structural reinforcement, and CROSS's novelty. The headline average gains remain 24.7 percentage points in MRR and 3.7 points in industrial node-classification AUC.

C2.justification: Appendix L.1 newly attributes semantic dynamics primarily to the prompting strategy. L.2 interprets edge-classification results as evidence of transferability while identifying a transfer-performance gap. The earlier conflicting-modality discussion and limitations concerning one-hop context and encoding choices are retained.

D1.justification: The new appendix experiments specify sampling variants, the frozen-encoder/two-layer-MLP setup, and reliance on DTGB configurations. Appendix D.2 removes the earlier explicit yes/no response-format description for the LLM baseline. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, API information, and conditional release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 2.2 explicitly contrasts TGNNs, LLM4GTAug methods, and CROSS by LLM usage and fusion stage. The bibliography adds eleven works, including SPEED, UniDyG, and DTFormer. The broader related-work organization and original novelty positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes Section 2 into preliminaries and related work, revises the temporal-reasoning introduction, expands Appendix L, and adds acknowledgments and author information. Most existing prose and the overall methodological narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the comparison schematic in Figure 2, the related-work summary table, and new experimental tables. The former combined AUC/Hits@10 table becomes separate expanded AP and AUC tables. All earlier figures are retained, with renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The additional metrics, targeted temporal ablations, and edge-classification experiments provide useful evidence beyond v2. However, the new Theorem 2 leaves its positive lower bound in Eq. 27 unjustified, and Table 1 reverses TGNN/LLM4GTAug properties relative to Section 2.2 and Figure 2. These empirical benefits and newly introduced correctness problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
